name: ULTIUM CELLS
entity_filed: Ultium Cells LLC (GM / LG Energy Solution joint venture)
same_company_evidence: Payee is the Detroit office of Ultium Cells LLC; the JobsOhio money went to the Lordstown, Ohio battery plant, which is the plant named in the coverage.
ohio_outcome: Ultium Cells cut 1,300 jobs at its Lordstown plant starting January 5, 2026, which the company tied to slower than expected electric vehicle demand. GM had announced the cuts on October 29, 2025 as part of about 3,300 job cuts across Michigan, Tennessee and Ohio. The plant stayed open. Recalls of laid-off workers were pushed from spring to August 2026, and workers began returning in late July and August 2026.
source: WFMJ 2026-01-05 'Ultium Cells cuts 1,300 jobs at Lordstown plant'; Business Journal Daily 2026-01-05; CNBC 2025-10-29; Reuters 2026-05-29; Business Journal Daily 2026-08-27 'Ultium Cells in Lordstown recalls laid-off workers'
notes: Largest cash grant in the batch, $50,000,000 in 2022 and 2023. The cut is a layoff, not a closure, and most of it has since been reversed. | The Ohio WARN notice breaks the 1,300 out as 484 permanent plus 850 temporary layoffs, effective 2026-01-05.

name: CASE WESTERN RESERVE UNIVERSITY
same_company_evidence: Same university, Cleveland, Ohio.
ohio_outcome: Nothing closed. The university shut its diversity office in March 2025 in response to a federal mandate, and a 2025 bomb threat canceled classes at the neighboring Cleveland Institute of Art. The campus and its research operations continue.
source: Ideastream 2025-03-26; Case Western Reserve University 2025-10-03
notes: Both flagged headlines use the word 'close' or 'shutting down' for something other than a business failure.

name: CLEVELAND STATE UNIVERSITY
same_company_evidence: Same university, Cleveland, Ohio.
ohio_outcome: The university laid off 14 staff and took more than 50 voluntary buyouts in August 2024 while closing a $40 million budget gap, and cut three sports in January 2025. It spent $9 million on buyouts. The university remains open and the grant-funded research operations continue.
source: WKYC 2024-08-20; Ideastream 2024-08-20; WKYC 2024-08-26; Cleveland.com 2024-04-09; Ideastream 2025-01-24
notes: Institution-wide budget cuts, not a closure or sale of the grant-funded operation.

name: GENERAL ELECTRIC COMPANY
same_company_evidence: Payee address is the Evendale, Ohio site, which is GE Aerospace headquarters.
ohio_outcome: GE Aviation detailed 605 layoffs at its Evendale headquarters in June 2020 during the pandemic collapse in air travel, after the first grant year of 2018. The site stayed open, kept receiving grants in 2023 and 2024, and in September 2026 GE Aerospace agreed to buy an Ohio supplier for $11.8 billion in a deal covering about 6,600 jobs.
source: The Business Journals 2020-06-23 'GE Aviation details 605 layoffs at Evendale headquarters'; FOX19 2020-06-23; Cincinnati Enquirer 2026-09-09
notes: The two flagged headlines were about Jacksonville, Florida and a ventilator campaign. The real Ohio cut is the 2020 Evendale layoff, which the site has since more than recovered from.

name: COVERMYMEDS LLC
same_company_evidence: Payee is in Columbus and the coverage names Columbus-based CoverMyMeds and its Franklinton headquarters.
ohio_outcome: CoverMyMeds cut 815 jobs on March 29, 2023, closed its Arizona office and put part of its Franklinton headquarters in Columbus up for sublease. Columbus staff were affected. It cut more positions in a restructuring announced March 30, 2026. The Columbus tax breaks it holds were challenged after the 2023 layoffs.
source: The Business Journals 2023-03-29 'CoverMyMeds cuts 815 jobs, will sublease portion of Franklinton HQ'; WOSU 2023-03-29; The Columbus Dispatch 2023-04-03 and 2023-03-31; The Columbus Dispatch 2026-03-30; WOSU 2026-03-30
notes: $6,613,235 across five grant years, 2017 through 2022. The 815-job cut is company-wide; the Ohio share was not broken out, but the sublease of the Columbus headquarters confirms the Ohio site shrank.

name: PAYCOR INC
same_company_evidence: Same Cincinnati payroll software company.
ohio_outcome: Nothing closed. Paycor was bought by Paychex of Rochester, New York for $4.1 billion, announced January 7, 2025 and completed in mid-April 2025. The Cincinnati operation continues and its move to a downtown Cincinnati headquarters was still going ahead into 2026.
source: WCPO 2025-01-07; Cincinnati Enquirer 2025-04-17; Democrat and Chronicle 2025-04-21; The Business Journals 2025-12-16
notes: The flagged headline was about auctioning suite furniture at Paycor Stadium, which is only a naming-rights tie. Worth noting as an ownership change: an Ohio grant recipient is now owned out of state.

name: NESTLE USA INC
same_company_evidence: Payee address is the Solon, Ohio campus, which is the site named in the closure announcement.
ohio_outcome: Nestlé will close its Solon factory by the end of 2027 and move production to South Carolina, announced October 19, 2026, affecting 370 jobs. The company says it will keep some presence in Solon. The Solon campus had already cut 77 jobs announced in November 2023 and about 200 to 216 more announced in late January 2024.
source: Cleveland.com 2026-10-19 'Nestlé to close Solon factory by end of 2027, move production to South Carolina'; Chagrin Valley Today 2026-10-22 '370 jobs affected'; Crain's Cleveland Business 2026-10-19; Akron Beacon Journal 2024-01-30; Cleveland.com 2023-11-06; Manufacturing Dive 2024-02-02
notes: Four grant years, 2016, 2018, 2020 and 2021, $3,200,000 total. The flagged headlines were about an Arlington, Virginia office foreclosure and a Taunton, Massachusetts closure, but the Solon site itself is closing. | No Ohio WARN notice exists yet for the 2027 Solon closure, which fits the timeline. Earlier Solon rounds do have notices: 77 jobs (2023-11-01) and 241 jobs (2024-01-29); the earlier reading said 'about 200 to 216' for the second.

name: DANA LIMITED
same_company_evidence: Payee is Dana's Maumee, Ohio headquarters, and the closing plant is in Lima, Ohio.
ohio_outcome: Dana is closing its Lima, Ohio driveshaft plant and laying off 295 workers, announced May 2, 2025. An earlier report in September 2024 put the figure at 280 jobs.
source: Toledo Blade 2025-05-02 'Dana to close Lima driveshaft plant, lay off 295 workers'; WTOL 2025-05-02; World Socialist Web Site 2024-09-01
notes: One grant year, 2019, $3,000,000. The closure is a different Ohio site from the Maumee headquarters that received the money.

name: PELLA CORPORATION
same_company_evidence: Payee is Pella Corporation of Pella, Iowa. Its Ohio project is the Troy plant announced in July 2020.
ohio_outcome: Nothing closed in Ohio. Pella's Ohio plant is in Troy, a 324,000 square foot factory with 428 jobs announced in July 2020, and no coverage reports a cut there. The closure is in Reidsville, North Carolina, where 133 jobs end.
source: The Business Journals 2026-10-19 'Pella Corp. shutting down Reidsville plant, eliminating 133 jobs'; 88.5 WFDD 2026-10-20; PR Newswire 2020-07-27; Dayton Daily News 2020-07-30
notes: Grant year 2022, $2,600,000. Closure is out of state.

name: HYLAND SOFTWARE INC
same_company_evidence: Payee is in Westlake, Ohio, and every story names Westlake-based Hyland Software.
ohio_outcome: Hyland laid off about 1,000 people, 20 percent of its workforce, announced April 3, 2023, which Crain's tied to the company's debt load. It had already cut more than 100 jobs in January 2021 while moving work to India and Poland. In August 2023 it listed two of its Westlake buildings for sale, and those buildings found their first new occupants in June 2026, so the Westlake footprint shrank.
source: Cleveland.com 2023-04-03; News 5 Cleveland 2023-04-03; Crain's Cleveland Business 2023-04-07; Cleveland.com 2023-08-07 'Hyland Software lists 2 Westlake properties'; Crain's Cleveland Business 2026-06-24; WKYC 2021-01-28
notes: Grant years 2018 and 2020, $2,500,001. The 1,000 figure is company-wide and the Ohio share was not disclosed, but the vacated Westlake buildings show the Ohio site contracted.

name: ABBOTT LABORATORIES
same_company_evidence: Payee is listed in Columbus; Abbott's Ohio project is the Bowling Green nutrition plant.
ohio_outcome: Nothing closed in Ohio. Abbott announced a $536 million powder formula plant in Bowling Green with 450 jobs in December 2022 and, as of November 2025, was still working on design and engineering with no new timeline. The layoffs in the flagged headlines were in the Bay Area, about 200 jobs, and elsewhere.
source: BG Independent News 2025-11-17 'Businesses have slowed at making commitments – but Abbott Labs is still planning to build in BG'; The Columbus Dispatch 2022-12-15; The Mercury News 2024-04-15
notes: Grant years 2023 and 2024, $2,500,000. Not a failure, but three years after the announcement the Ohio plant has not been built and has no public timeline.

name: SAREPTA THERAPEUTICS
same_company_evidence: Payee is the Cambridge, Massachusetts headquarters; the Ohio operation is the Columbus area gene therapy site, and the coverage names Franklin County.
ohio_outcome: Sarepta cut 80 jobs in Franklin County, Ohio, announced July 18, 2025, as part of about 500 cuts company-wide after a gene therapy safety setback.
source: 10TV 2025-07-18 'Sarepta Therapeutics laying off nearly 500 employees, including 80 in Franklin County'; WSYX 2025-07-18; The Columbus Dispatch 2025-07-21; The Business Journals 2025-07-16
notes: Grant years 2021, 2022 and 2023, $2,348,087. The Ohio site was not closed. | The Ohio figure of 80 is in the state WARN notice, and the company-wide restructuring is in an 8-K filed the same day under Item 2.05.

name: CROWN EQUIPMENT CORPORATION
same_company_evidence: Payee is Crown's New Bremen, Ohio headquarters, the location named in the coverage.
ohio_outcome: Crown offered a voluntary layoff program to employees at New Bremen in January 2020, after the 2019 grant year. No job count was published, the program was voluntary, and Crown received another grant in 2023, so the Ohio operation continues.
source: Sidney Daily News 2020-01-07 'Crown begins voluntary layoffs'; The Business Journals 2020-01-07; Mercer County Outlook 2020-01-07
notes: Grant years 2019 and 2023, $2,229,000. Crown had announced 563 new full-time positions in November 2018.

name: SPEEDWAY LLC
entity_filed: Speedway LLC (sold by Marathon Petroleum to 7-Eleven)
same_company_evidence: Payee is the Enon, Ohio headquarters named in the Springfield News-Sun and WHIO coverage.
ohio_outcome: Marathon Petroleum sold Speedway to 7-Eleven for $21 billion in May 2021, the year of the last grant. 7-Eleven then cut fewer than 35 jobs at the Enon headquarters in October 2021 and cut more Enon staff in July 2022 as part of about 880 corporate job cuts tied to the Speedway integration.
source: Springfield News-Sun 2021-10-11 and 2021-10-13; Convenience Store News 2021-10-12; WHIO TV 2022-07-22; Springfield News-Sun 2022-07-22; Business Insider 2022-07-22
notes: Grant years 2018, 2020 and 2021, $1,700,000. The Ohio operation was sold out of state and the Enon headquarters was cut down during the integration; the exact Enon job count for 2022 was not published.

name: TRACTOR SUPPLY COMPANY
same_company_evidence: Payee is Tractor Supply's Brentwood, Tennessee headquarters; its Ohio project is the Navarre distribution center.
ohio_outcome: Nothing closed in Ohio. The $70 million Navarre, Ohio distribution center, the company's largest, opened in January 2023 and is still operating. The flagged headlines are about closing 75 Petsense pet stores across the chain.
source: Canton Repository 2023-01-18; Tractor Supply 2023-01-18; CoStar 2026-07-23; The Hill 2026-08-04
notes: Grant year 2021, $1,500,000. Petsense is a separate retail brand.

name: GENERAL MILLS INC
same_company_evidence: Payee is the Minneapolis headquarters; the Ohio operation is the Wellston Totino's pizza plant in Jackson County.
ohio_outcome: Nothing closed in Ohio. General Mills put $100 million into the Wellston plant in 2022 with 30 added jobs, and a further $70 million expansion was under way as of November 2025. The closures are in Missouri: three plants announced October 2025 and the St. Charles plant with more than 150 jobs lost in 2026.
source: JobsOhio 2022-08-29; Food Dive 2025-10-01; Industrial Info Resources 2025-11-26; KSDK 2026-04-06; FOX 2 2026-04-06

name: ST BERNARD SOAP COMPANY
entity_filed: St. Bernard Soap Company (Trillium Health Care Products)
same_company_evidence: Payee is in Cincinnati, and the plant is the former Procter & Gamble soap works in St. Bernard, Ohio.
ohio_outcome: St. Bernard Soap announced on January 4, 2024 that it would close the plant permanently in March 2024, terminating 118 employees, months after laying off more than 100. The site, at P&G's old Ivorydale works, has since been floated for a data center. In December 2024 a court ordered the tenants of the building to pay about $30 to $32 million in unpaid rent and utilities, and in February 2024 the property owed nearly $1.8 million in unpaid bills.
source: WLWT 2024-01-04 'St. Bernard Soap Company closing plant, terminating 118 employees'; Cincinnati Enquirer 2024-01-04; The Business Journals 2024-01-04; Cincinnati Enquirer 2024-12-09; WLWT 2024-12-10; The Business Journals 2024-02-28
notes: Grant year 2019, $900,000. The plant closed about five years after the grant.

name: MRI SOFTWARE
same_company_evidence: Payee is in Solon, Ohio, and Propmodo describes MRI Software as Ohio-based; Crain's Cleveland Business reported the cuts locally.
ohio_outcome: MRI Software eliminated about 200 positions in a global reorganization reported May 11, 2026, which it tied to AI adoption. It would not say how many were affected or where, and it does not break out how many of its 5,000-plus staff work in Northeast Ohio. The Solon operation continues. Its private equity owners hired Goldman Sachs in September 2025 to explore a sale valuing the company at up to $10 billion.
source: Crain's Cleveland Business 2026-05-11 'Layoffs reportedly hit MRI Software'; Propmodo 2026-05-11 'Private Equity-Backed Proptech Firm Cuts 200 Jobs, Cites AI Adoption'
notes: Grant years 2018, 2019 and 2021, $800,000. The Ohio share of the 200 cuts is not public, so I could not settle how much of this landed in Solon.

name: US BANK NATIONAL ASSOCIATION
same_company_evidence: Payee is the U.S. Bancorp headquarters in Minneapolis. The foreclosure stories concern U.S. Bank acting as trustee in other people's mortgage cases, not the bank failing.
ohio_outcome: Nothing closed. U.S. Bank cut 65 Cincinnati jobs in February 2020, after the 2019 grant, and was closing some Cincinnati branches as of July 2026. The bank continues to operate in Ohio and received another grant in 2023.
source: The Business Journals 2020-02-11 'U.S. Bank to lay off 65 Cincinnati employees'; WKRC 2026-07-19; Mortgage Professional America 2025-12-12 and 2026-05-07
notes: Grant years 2019 and 2023, $800,000. Both flagged headlines are the classic false positive: a bank named as plaintiff or trustee in someone else's foreclosure.

name: OVERDRIVE INC
same_company_evidence: Same Cleveland-area digital library company, maker of the Libby and Sora apps.
ohio_outcome: Nothing closed. The headline is about OverDrive's trademark suit against OpenAI over the name Sora, filed in November 2025; OpenAI is the one shutting its Sora product down. OverDrive continues to operate in Ohio.
source: Reuters 2025-11-20; Publishers Weekly 2025-11-20; Crain's Cleveland Business 2025-11-25 and 2026-04-08
notes: Grant years 2020 and 2024, $800,000. 'Shutting down' in the headline refers to OpenAI's product, not OverDrive.

name: P GRAHAM DUNN INC
same_company_evidence: Payee is in Dalton, Ohio, the town where the campus was sold and the jobs were cut.
ohio_outcome: P. Graham Dunn announced on October 2, 2024 that it was closing, laying off employees and moving out of Dalton, blaming the retail market. Its Dalton campus was sold to ProVia, which had announced the purchase of two Dalton properties in July 2024 and was building a new facility there by 2025. The business itself was acquired by Creative Brands in October 2024. No job count was published.
source: Canton Repository 2024-10-02 'P. Graham Dunn closing, lays off employees; property sale to ProVia should close this year'; The Business Journals 2024-10-04; Wooster Daily Record 2024-07-18; Plastics News 2024-07-17; Smart Business Dealmakers 2024-10-08 'Creative Brands Acquires P. Graham Dunn'
notes: Grant years 2017 and 2021, $790,000. Both a closure of the Dalton operation and a sale of the company; I could not find a jobs figure in any available source. | The jobs figure is now sourced: the Ohio WARN notice gives 92 affected at Dalton, Wayne County, effective 2024-10-20.

name: Hunter Defense Technologies Inc
same_company_evidence: Payee is in Solon, Ohio, which is the company headquarters; the closing plant is in Florence, Kentucky.
ohio_outcome: Nothing closed in Ohio. The mass layoff notice was in Kentucky, closing the Florence facility and cutting 94 jobs in June 2024. The company, now trading as BLADE/HDT Global, is still active and won new defense contracts in October 2026.
source: The Business Journals 2024-06-03; WKRC 2024-06-03 'Manufacturer to close NKY facility, lay off 94 employees'; The Defense Post 2026-10-14; hdtglobal.com news page, read 2026-11-03
notes: Grant year 2016, $750,000. The Florence plant was the one that added 113 jobs in 2018, on the Kentucky side of the Cincinnati line.
